Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-01
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Jamie Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (CTO, Astral IO), Dan Brooks (Sr ML Eng), Sara Kim (Product)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Short discovery focused on PLG/self-serve path, time-to-first-token, free credits, and which workloads would benefit from hosted vs dedicated/private. Customer emphasized compliance and latency SLOs for interactive chat. Next steps: send quickstart, run quick benchmark, provide sample prompts, schedule deep dive if needed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. We also have Jamie our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:05] Maya: Good, thanks. Maya here. We were excited to learn more about the quickstart, been poking at the docs but wanted to get a sense of time to first token and what the PLG flow looks like.
[00:12] Alex: Perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Quick agenda: quick intro, PLG/self-serve flow, free credits and onboarding, then a couple of qualification questions around security and scale, and finally next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Dan: Yep sounds good.
[00:20] Sara: Yep.
[00:24] Jamie: I'll jump in on the technical bits and run through an example request path.

[00:30] Alex: Cool. So the PLG path is pretty straightforward — sign up, you get free credits, use the Redwood API (we have SDKs for Python, JS), you can send a request to hosted models and be generating tokens within minutes. Typical time-to-first-token for teams that follow our quickstart is 5-15 minutes if you already have a prompt set. If you need to connect to internal data sources that's where dedicated or private comes in.
[00:50] Maya: When you say free credits, how much and do they require a card? Also do they expire?
[00:55] Alex: Good question. For the PLG quickstart we grant $500 in credits for new accounts aimed at experimentation. Card optional for initial signup, required if you want to extend beyond credits. Credits expire in 90 days. We'll include the exact redemption link and policy in the email.
[01:10] Dan: And the hosted models — are you running open models or proprietary models? We care about inference quality and latency.
[01:15] Jamie: We operate a catalog: curated open models plus our verified performance profiles. Hosted API gives you a selection of tuned open models and model variants (quantized and full precision). We also provide latency and token-cost estimates per model. For chat at  request sizes you described earlier, you can expect p95 latency in the 200-400ms range for small context windows on our hosted plan, depends on model choice and tokenization.
[01:42] Maya: Is that p95 for generation or end-to-end? Because our SLA needs p95 end-to-end under 500ms.
[01:47] Jamie: That's generation time from send to first token; end-to-end including network usually fits under 500ms for many models in the catalog in our US regions. We can run a benchmark with your prompt set to be sure.
[01:58] Sara: About integration—what's the quickest path to embed into our product? We want a server-side call in Node for chat.
[02:03] Alex: The SDK is a 2-3 line call; we'll send a sample quickstart repo. Time-to-first-token from a dev who follows the repo is typically under 10 minutes.

[02:12] Dan: Security is big for us. We need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and enterprise key management eventually. Does Redwood support those on PLG?
[02:22] Alex: For the hosted PLG tier, SOC 2 alignment and SOC2 report is available for customers under NDA — we can share the attestation. SSO/SAML and enterprise KMS are part of our paid enterprise features and are available on Dedicated and Private. For PLG self-serve you get basic API keys and usage logging; dedicated gives you VPC and customer-managed KMS.
[02:40] Maya: So if our initial proof of concept starts on hosted PLG, would it be painful to move to Dedicated later?
[02:46] Jamie: We built migration paths for that — same API and SDKs, you can pin model versions and change your deployment mode with minimal app changes. The main lift is in networking (VPC peering) and onboarding security controls.
[02:58] Sara: Any issues around data retention — we need logs retained for 12 months for product telemetry, but customer data should be purged after 30 days.
[03:06] Alex: We have configurable retention; by default hosted PLG keeps logs 30 days, but enterprise/paid plans can opt-in for longer retention and different retention rules. We'll include retention policy docs.
[03:16] Maya: What about private on-prem? We might go that route for regulated customers.
[03:19] Jamie: Private gives you control plane inside your VPC or even on-prem. We support an on-prem package that runs behind your firewall — that comes with additional support and licensing.

[03:28] Alex: Quick qualification — what's your timeline and success criteria?
[03:32] Maya: Timeline is a 2-3 month proof of concept, then decide by quarter end. Success looks like: 1) integration with product, 2) p95 end-to-end <500ms for interactive chat, 3) cost estimate under our target (we have a cost per 1k tokens target), and 4) compliance checklist pass for SOC/ISO items.
[03:50] Alex: Great, that's doable. We'll prioritize a hosted quickstart + benchmark for the latency/cost measurement.

[03:58] Dan: One other question: do you support streaming responses and tool/function calling? We use tool-calling to fetch data during a chat.
[04:05] Jamie: Yes, streaming is supported by the API and we've got first-class function-calling patterns in our SDK. We'll share a short example.

[04:12] Sara: Any common gotchas for teams doing the PLG path?
[04:16] Alex: A couple: 1) watch prompt engineering and tokenization — token costs can spike with long system prompts; 2) ensure you cache static prefixes or use caching features; 3) choose the model variant that balances cost/latency — we'll help.

[04:28] Maya: Who is the contact for support during the quickstart?
[04:31] Alex: I'll be your AE, and Jamie will handle technical support. For PLG self-serve you also have docs and community resources; for POCs we'll set up a short Slack channel or email thread.

[04:40] Alex: Jamie, could you outline the benchmark you'd run?
[04:43] Jamie: Sure. We'll take the 3 sample prompts you provide, run them across 3 model variants (base open, quantized, and our latency-optimized variant) over a 30-minute synthetic load to get p50/p95/p99 and token cost. We'll also measure cold start behavior and prefix caching impact. We can do that on hosted infra and show what a Dedicated reservation looks like for that throughput.

[05:05] Dan: Do you have an example pricing estimate for small-mid scale — say 20k tokens/day?
[05:10] Alex: Roughly, on hosted plans at current list rates it's in the low hundreds per month for 20k tokens depending on model. We'll send a detailed cost estimate — Jamie will attach the benchmark spreadsheet so you can tweak numbers.

[05:22] Maya: Any regulatory regions? We need EU data residency for some clients.
[05:26] Jamie: We have EU regions and can route requests to region-specific endpoints. For strict residency and on-prem, Private is recommended.

[05:34] Sara: Are there case studies for teams that started PLG then moved to Dedicated?
[05:38] Alex: Yes, we'll share a short case study about a SaaS company that started on PLG and moved to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower unit cost — I'll include that link.

[05:47] Maya: Great. A couple of more technical items — do you support KMS integrations like AWS KMS / Google KMS and HSM for keys at rest?
[05:56] Jamie: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys; HSM options available for on-prem enterprise.

[06:05] Dan: For model variants, do you support quantized runtimes and what are the typical memory/cost savings?
[06:10] Jamie: We do. Quantized variants generally reduce GPU memory by ~30-60% and can cut token-cost by a similar margin depending on batch and precision, though latency characteristics vary. We'll show real numbers in the benchmark.

[06:24] Alex: Ok i'm going to recap next steps — we will: 1) send PLG quickstart repo and redemption link for $500 credits; 2) Jamie will run a hosted benchmark using the prompts you supply; 3) we'll send security/compliance docs (SOC2, data retention, SSO notes); 4) schedule a technical deep dive if dedicated/private looks needed. Anything to add?
[06:44] Maya: That covers it. We'll try to get the prompts and compliance checklist to you by May 6.
[06:49] Sara: Could you also include sample code for streaming responses to Node?
[06:52] Jamie: Yes will include code snippets and a mini-repo.

[06:57] Alex: Awesome. Anything else from the team?
[06:59] Dan: No, that's all.
[07:01] Maya: Thanks all.
[07:02] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with the materials.

[07:06] --- End of meeting ---

Notes on transcription imperfections: occasional speaker ID mismatch and word substitution expected (e.g., 'KV cache' transcribed as 'key V cache' in some parts of the call). Timestamps approximate every few minutes.
